item.title: You're It (SCP concept): You're It (SCP concept)
item.content:encoded:
An affliction that causes individuals to attack others and pass on the affliction to survivors of the attacks. Those affected by this SCP will cease to be afflicted after passing it on.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

This SCP is a phenomenon that causes afflicted individuals to quickly become more hostile and violent towards others, as well as giving them increased physical strength and resistance to injury. The exact cause of this is unknown, as no pathogen or other potential source has yet to be identified. This SCP will likely cause affected individuals to attack nearby people, often resulting in their deaths. Those who survive these attacks will begin to exhibit the same anomalous effects as their attacker, while the attacker will slowly lose the aggression and increased strength.

Those that have "passed on" the SCP have a moderate chance to die of multiple organ failure after the effects have subsided, and those that live retain memories of their actions while under the influence of this SCP. Should the current carrier of this SCP die before passing it on, it will instead be passed on to the carrier's killer. If the carrier was not killed by a sapient being, the SCP will instead pass on to a random individual, where nearer individuals are more likely to be afflicted.

This SCP is contained via an afflicted D-Class personnel inside a reinforced concrete humanoid containment chamber. The D-Class is kept alive as long as possible, and their vitals are constantly monitored. Additional D-Class personnel are introduced into the chamber to allow the SCP to be passed on. The previous carrier will be tranquilized via remotely controlled sentries before they can kill the new carrier. The previous carrier, now sedated, is removed from the chamber and amnestics are administered.

item.title: Heartbeat of Iceland: Heartbeat of Iceland
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Horror

Page Layout: ACS header, basic layout, tons of audio recordings and exploration logs

Elevator Pitch: Series of sounds that resemble heartbeats, only found in deep lakes in Iceland, each with varying frequencies and loudness. The sounds are quite rare and cause mishaps in reality in a wide area around it.

Central Narrative: The heartbeats last for 20-75 seconds, and range in frequency, loudness, and location. Heartbeats are relatively rare (1-3 times a year) but can be very troubling for the area around it.

Heartbeats come in pairs of 2 "pumps", in this case, sound. Once a heartbeat starts, the pumps cause vibrations in the land, seemingly wavy land. Everything the sound can be heard is effected.
Here's a list of each possible reality-bending scenario

  • Vibrations in the land (wavy-like land)
  • Mountains deforming in a very unnatural way
  • Water vortexes
  • "cracks" in the air, where a black spot fills the crack
  • Clouds taking shape of humanoid figures
  • Talbon's Ring (a high-frequency ring that burst eardrums and rarely kills an organism)
  • The sky turning into dark, even during bright days
  • Temperature suddenly shooting up or increasing drastically
  • Altered heartbeats of humans (matches the lake's heartbeat)

These are the only known effects of the heartbeat, but in later logs, more will appear (creepier and deadlier). A heartbeat can have serious effects on the ecosystem, and cause mass death amongst organisms, and heavily deformed land.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A decent reality-bender that has some good potential, even though it probably has a LOT to work on.

Additional Notes: Suggestions for editing needed :)

item.title: Counting Sheep: Counting Sheep
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-fi

Page Layout: An SCP Article that has collapsible sections with up to date versions of the SCP’s description, containment procedures and so on. (This is necessary due to the nature of this SCP.)

Elevator Pitch: A herd of nine migrating sheep (SCP-XXXX-1) that causes sudden and inexplicable somnolence for subjects inside a 1km spherical radius. The herd exhibits no biological anomalies with the exception that none seem to need sustenance nor excrete waste, and at the time of discovery seemed to be in a pattern of continuous migration. The nine sheep are living embodiments of nine identical music boxes that contain the mental essence of a child that suffered from fatal familial insomnia.

Central Narrative: The SCP was brought to the foundation's attention after a 2km chain car crash happened on a highway caused by the sudden onset of fatigue of multiple drivers. The foundation successfully captured the herd by estimating and setting up traps along its migratory route. SCP-XXXX is contained within a circular metal fence to prevent unauthorized personnel from entering SCP-XXXX-1’s effective radius.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-1 transformed into SCP-XXXX-2, a set of nine identical music boxes a month into containment. However, when music was played from all nine boxes simultaneously, they transformed back. The discovery of SCP-XXXX-2’s abilities led to the Slumbering Prison Incident at the foundation where the SCP placed all living organisms on the site which SCP-XXXX was contained under a state of somnolence. During the incident, all nine sheep broke out of the facility and began retracing their steps back to their place of origin. Before a team could be mobilized, all the sheep stopped in front of a small house on the edge of a city. When a team of SCP agents got there, all the sheep turned back into music boxes. Inside of all the boxes, there was a new engraving that says “Mom, I am home.”

The last owner of the house was a single mother with a son whose dreams of being an adventurer is shattered by fatal familial insomnia. The son started to develop symptoms at the age of 6 and was bedridden until he died at the age of 15. The mother went missing a month after the death of her son. Video recordings were found of the mother giving the son one music box that looks identical to one instance of SCP-XXXX-2 during his birthday. Every year he suffered from insomnia, he was given the same music box.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This story is about a child chasing his dream and his relationship with his mother makes it interesting.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.: Re: [Seeking Greenlight] Host of the Eldritch Abomination.
item.content:encoded:
Hello GodlyUser! let's take a look :)

ONE SANDY BOI

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A teenager name "Janual Grey" discovers that he's no longer a human after an unexplained blackout while camping at Acadia National Park, and later on woke up and finds himself as a reality-altering eldritch abomination.

This sounds like a good setup, but there isn't much done with it throughout the narrative and the rest of the concept. Nothing really expands on what happens to the skip itself or how that affects him. Along with this, there much explaining what the blackout did to cause this, or what caused him to fall asleep.- did this happen while he was asleep? did the blackout cause him to fall asleep?

Discovering his powers has made a few changes in him. Janual possesses numerous anomalous properties that not even he knows how many he has and every 24 hours. If Janual doesn't consume any food, he will get driven into a state of absolute hostility, where he would go on a never-ending frenzy to satisfy his hunger, which of course that time he would begin to use more of his anomalous properties to lure humans deep into the woods. This is why he usually lures bad peoples into his territory and consumes them; this is a nature he embodies.

This feels a bit overcomplicated, the effects shown here (and their progression) are fairly specific, how would this look in an article? how do the characters and Foundation learn about this 24hr rule? why does this happen at 24hrs specifically? how is it stoped?

Another thing I have an issue with is the sheer amount of anomalies the skip has, if there are so many effects that not all of them can be mentioned, then there are too many. I would highly recommend you simplify this down to one or two main anomalies, as it keeps the narrative and concept simple and doesn't cause the skip become overpowered as easily.

The narrative:

Janual wasn't actually a human at all from the start. His father is an eldritch abomination worshiped by a cult named "Servants of "Darkness" " secretly built under a church where the cult mainly focuses on worshiping a deity named "Darkness". When the cult managed to summon his father after offering a sacrifice as a deadman's body, it manifested itself into the body. It seduced Janual's mother into having a child when she visits the church during Christmas with Janual's grandmother. After borning out Janual, his father de-manifest itself out of reality to let its son, Janual, destroy the world instead of it. However, due to embodying some human natures, Janual didn't become malevolent as his father was.

Overall, this feels closer to an explanation than it does a narrative, how would the current narrative fit into an article? how does the Foundation learn about this?-whats the build up to this discovery? does the skip ever learn of this?- how does that make him feel (assuming he does eventually learn of it)?

Along with this, the "the mother is this and the father is that, this is their child" premise, feels a bit cliched to me. As the concept and narrative don't currently offer anything new to the premise, which as a result, makes everything feel a bit flat.- what makes this stand out from similar ideas?

After a few years, Janual's mother witnessed him eating their next-door neighbors in his monstrous form at 3 years old. As she started to find answers to why her son is like this, she soon discovers the truth while reading some books about gods, ancient myths, and satanic traits, including mythos of different beings. She even surfs the web for information and soon found the truth. She knows what she must do. She must find a way to seal his powers from being unleashed due to worrying that he might bring apocalyptic events and was successfully to be able to seal it. However, during the past years, she slowly forgets about it.

This still feels closer to an explanation, there isn't any clear setup, middle act, payoff and conflict here. what actually happens in the story? how does this affect the skip itself?

-small nitpick: the murder of the neighbours isn't really mentioned again, how is that covered up?

The Foundation doesn't really get a mention here either, which confuses me as the article would be written from their perspective. How do they find the skip originally? how is it contained? what do they learn about it? who are the main characters (assuming some are researchers)? what is the main conflict? how does the narrative end? how will this story make me as the reader feel?

Generally thoughts:
Overall, the skip itself isn't really given enough focus in the narrative or concept, and due to the amount of effects it currently has, it feels closer to a comic book character as there isn't any motives or clear focus shown. Along with this, the narrative comes off as an explanation rather than a narrative.- how will all of this fit into an article? what is the progression of events? whats everything building up to?

Overall, I would recommend simplifying the idea down (get rid of anything that doesn't contribute to the main idea, or would be irrelevant to the concept and narratives progression overall), find one main focus and one or two effects for the skip and build the narrative around that.- as a quick note: make sure the effects relate to the skip and each other.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Janual is a friend in school with SCP-105 before being held in Foundation custody.

This isn't really a hook, as it isn't related to the rest of the concept, its not brought up anywhere else, nor does it play any role in the story. The hook is the main idea of the concept/narrative, the part that will make the reader invested. Generally, you're looking to put the core idea or main focus of your concept/narrative in the hook.

-as a second note, I wouldn't recommend referencing series one articles, as it takes focus away from your skip and can come across as a way to quickly gain attention. If you're interested in cross linking, I would recommend only looking at the more recent series (5 and 6).

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no greenlight

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: In the blink of an eye: Re: In the blink of an eye
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via pm
Hello! Interesting SCP you've got there!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

Imma be honest..I kinda like this idea!
The only thing is I'm not sure if the Foundation would be the one too something like this. Combining humans with anomalous items seems something more like a Sarkic thing to do. Maybe the Agent gets left behind/capture during a raid on a Sarkic base, resulting in a ritual/experiment on her being performed that gives her those eyes? You can choose to keep/reject its idea, but just make sure it remains belivable.
My other concern is that the agent might become a bit omnipotent, so I think you should give some sort of consequence to her power and/or make them less strong. Maybe she starts to go insane or looses her free will/higher brain function, reducing her to little more than a mindless robot used by the foundation to do their dirty work.
I'm really close to greenlighting this. If you can just fix those two concerns, I'm more than willing to give you the go ahead. Best of luck, and please PM me if you want me to take another look!

item.title: House of Memories: Re: House of Memories
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via pm
That's an interesting SCP you've got there!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

I'll be honest and upfront about this idea: it seems really wishy-washy, and as Plague said in his reply, you're not going in a singe concise direction. You need to reign in you story, and focus on one particular aspect of it. Aside from that, there are some plot points that really do irk me. HEre are a few concerns I have:

  • Origin: So, a kid's grandmother just happens to know a spell that can curse households? It seems really out of the blue, and it doesn't really seem like you thought your concept through. I get each scp doesn't need to have a clear origin or discovery story, but what you have just seems too random for my liking.
  • Cliche: It's clear your trying to evoke some emotional response in your audience, specifically fear, but the way you're describing it right now just doesn't fit. There's a lot of SCPs on this site that deal with past traumas/memories. While no concept is 100% unique and original, yours does rely too much on pre-existing tropes
  • Believability: I highly doubt that the Foundation would Raise kids for the sole purpose of making them into D-Class. That's not how the Foundation works. More than likely, the kids would be amnesticized and released into society, killed if they are too dangerous to be kept around (which I doubt would happen), or classified as SCPs themselves.

You really need to tighten up your story. It's fine if you take a couple days to reply or edit your response: you just need to ensure that it's something appealing to your audience, including your critiquers. As of right now, no greenlight, but if you want me to come take another look, do PM me!
Best of luck
